facts.fact_text: All three applicants decided to hold solo demonstrations on 19 December 2012.
According to the applicants, at around 9 a.m. on 19 December 2012 they positioned themselves, holding banners, in the vicinity of the State Duma.
According to the applicants, at around 9 a.m. on 19 December 2012 they were positioned at some distance from other protesters in the vicinity of the State Duma.
According to the first applicant (Ms Makarova), she was arrested by the police several minutes after positioning herself near the State Duma on 19 December 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Makarova), there were no orders from police officers to stop the demonstration and leave the area before her arrest.

According to the second applicant (Ms Astakhova) and the third applicant (Ms Fokht-Babushkina), after their solo demonstrations they left the area, showing their posters to journalists at the journalists' request.
According to the second applicant (Ms Astakhova) and the third applicant (Ms Fokht-Babushkina), at the point when they were showing their posters to journalists, they were arrested by the police.
According to the first applicant (Ms Makarova), she was arrested by the police several minutes after positioning herself near the State Duma on 19 December 2012.
According to the second applicant (Ms Astakhova) and the third applicant (Ms Fokht-Babushkina), at the point when they were showing their posters to journalists, they were arrested by the police.

According to the Government, at 10.30 a.m. on 19 December 2012 the applicants were arrested and taken to the Tverskoy district police station for the purpose of compiling an administrative-offence record.

At the Tverskoy district police station the applicants were charged with participating in a group public event held without prior notification, in breach of Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

A summary of domestic law and practice concerning regulations relating to the conduct of public events, liability for breaches committed in the course of such events, and administrative escorting and arrest can be found in Lashmankin and Others v. Russia, nos. 57818/09 and 14 others, §§ 216-312, 7 February 2017.

A summary of domestic law and practice concerning regulations relating to the conduct of public events, liability for breaches committed in the course of such events, and administrative escorting and arrest can also be found in Novikova and Others v. Russia, nos. 25501/07 and 4 others, §§ 47-84, 26 April 2016.

Until 1 January 2013, charges under Article 20.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences were to be determined at first instance by a justice of the peace, pursuant to Article 23.1 § 3 of the Code of Administrative Offences as in force until 1 January 2013.

Since 1 January 2013, charges under Article 20.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences are to be determined at first instance by a district court of general jurisdiction, pursuant to Article 23.1 § 3 of the Code of Administrative Offences as in force since 1 January 2013.

At the Tverskoy district police station the applicants were charged with participating in a group public event held without prior notification, in breach of Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
According to the Government, at 10 a.m. on 19 December 2012 all three applicants took part in a group picket (пикет) held without prior notification of the authorities.
According to the Government, the applicants did not react to the lawful demands of the police to stop participating in the group picket on 19 December 2012.
According to the Government, the applicants continued picketing and attracted the attention of passers-by on 19 December 2012.

The administrative-offence record and police officers' reports stated that the applicants had taken part in a non-notified group public event and had refused to end it when requested to do so by the police.

The justice of the peace found it established, on the basis of the administrative-offence record, the police officers' reports, and oral testimony by a police officer who had arrested the first applicant (Ms Makarova), that the first applicant had taken part in a public event (picket) which had involved fifty people and had been held without prior notification of the authorities.
